subject: Anchoring & variance deconflict — evidence request and alignment steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@peopleops.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Anchoring & variance deconflict — evidence request and alignment steps

Morning all,

We saw a few clusters in the Q2 distributions that are driving downstream disagreement across teams (more mid-to-upper bands than expected for a couple of org slices). I want to run a short, focused alignment so we have a clear, evidence-driven path to resolve anchors and variance before final HR handoff.

My ask is threefold:
1) Laura / Marissa — please pull the sample set for the 6 folks flagged in the "high-variance" bucket and include 2 manager notes + one peer note each. Save as calibration_evidence.csv and drop in the shared Drive folder (link below).
2) Stephanie — can you synthesize the rubric differences you used vs the cross-team rubric and call out where weighting diverges (brief table, 1 page).
3) Karthik — please confirm whether any of these engineers were under role or scope changes this cycle (brief yes/no + note).

Timeline: can we get the artifacts uploaded by EOD Wednesday so Nicole and I can pre-read? I’ll schedule a 45-minute alignment on Thursday 10am PT to adjudicate anchors and, where necessary, suggest counter-evidence or an exception path.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExample/Calibration-Q2
JIRA: PERF-9823

Attachments: redwood_calibration_template.xlsx (template for evidence capture)

Thanks — keep it tight and factual; we’re trying to limit HR escalations and avoid mass re-buckets.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product & Research Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring & variance deconflict — evidence request and alignment steps

Hannah — on it. I pulled the six profiles (IDs attached in calibration_evidence.csv) and included manager notes from their most recent 1:1s plus one peer snippet per person where available. Two quick flags:
- One engineer switched from product-facing infra to platform late March; I marked that row with "scope_change".
- For one manager, their notes are terse — I added a short synthesis and included commit history links.

I uploaded calibration_evidence.csv and manager_anchor_notes.docx to the Drive folder. See the files in the attachment list below.

Attachments referenced: calibration_evidence.csv, manager_anchor_notes.docx

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Eng Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring & variance deconflict — evidence request and alignment steps

Thanks — uploaded a 1-page rubric divergence note to the Drive (file: rubric_delta_summary.pdf). Short version here:
- Our rubric gives slightly more weight to cross-team impact and longitudinal delivery consistency (30% vs 20%).
- Other teams leaned more on current-quarter scope achievement (40% vs our 25%).
- Biggest practical effect: engineers with steady delivery but intermittent cross-team influence land higher on our curve; the inverse lands higher in orgs emphasizing single-Q impact.

Recommendation for the Thursday session: use a two-axis view (consistency x impact) for the six cases and explicitly call out where weighting caused the bucket divergence — that should make counter-evidence assessment straightforward.

Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal, Program Management
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@peopleops.com>
Date: Thu, 25 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring & variance deconflict — evidence request and alignment steps

Looping in a quick thought before the meeting: for any case where a manager wants to move a band up based on counter-evidence, we should require both a documented behavioral anchor (from the rubric) and one corroborating peer example. That reduces subjective inflation and makes HR signoff faster. Nicole, does that match People Ops' tolerance?

On attachments: I also added two peer excerpts into the Drive under "peer_snippets/" and flagged which ones meet the corroboration rule.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, People Science
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation from People Ops: the corroboration rule that Marissa suggested (behavioral anchor + peer corroboration) is acceptable for upward band exceptions, provided the packet includes a timeline of the behaviors and two distinct corroborators (can be manager+peer or peer+peer). Please ensure any redlines to banding are recorded in the JIRA ticket (PERF-9823) and route the final packet to peopleops-exceptions@redwoodinference.com.

I’ll plan to join the Thursday 10am PT call as an observer. If you expect a sensitive escalation that needs pre-consult, ping me directly and I’ll carve time before the meeting.

Nicole Park
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference
